props.title: Jahmyr Gibbs OVER 29.5 receiving yards
props.cutoff: OVER 29.5 at -115 or better only; pass at 30.5+ or -116 and worse. Reverify the live price after expiry.
props.edge: Projected mean +3.5 yards, not a probability edge. Uncalibrated judgment: about 55% to clear, versus 53.49% break-even at -115 (about +1.5 percentage points; about +2.8% expected return if that estimate is right). Plausible 50–60% uncertainty includes negative value.
props.why: The verified 29.5-yard number is below his 34.4 last-five and 44.9 last-ten averages. Five targets and 30 receiving yards in Week 1 support continuing receiving involvement; the team confirms an expanded lead-back role. My conservative 33-yard projection uses 5.5 targets × 75% catches × 8 yards per catch, below the recent target averages. Buffalo favored by 5.5 gives a plausible passing script. Detroit line absences may encourage outlets, but that is an inference, not the main reason.
props.risk: Thin estimated edge and uncertain routes under a new coordinator. Missing Mahogany and Miller could require Gibbs to block instead. Buffalo held Houston RBs to four catches for 17 yards last week; that one game does not prove a favorable matchup. Overtime inflated Week 1 touches. Inactives and wind remain pregame checks; no unsupported weather or scheme boost.

gameWatch.title: Jahmyr Gibbs receptions · OVER candidate
gameWatch.quoteNote: Viewed directly Sep 17, 11:33 AM ET. Earlier BetMGM 3.5 was an article at a different book; this is not proven same-book movement.
gameWatch.why: Pass on the receptions over at this check: five catches are now required in the observed DraftKings market. Receiving yards 29.5 is the chosen official favorite instead. The two markets should not be stacked as independent picks.
gameWatch.defense: Compare Buffalo pressure with Detroit routes versus pass-blocking assignments. Buffalo lists Cole Bishop and T.J. Sanders questionable; their availability could change coverage and pressure. A favorable reception matchup is not established yet.
gameWatch.lineHealth: Detroit ruled out Christian Mahogany (hip) and Blake Miller (knee) on Sep 16. Juice Scruggs finished full participation without a game designation. Confirm replacements and game-day inactives.
gameWatch.lineSkill: Detroit’s Sep 14 report described Ben Bartch’s first game as uneven, citing one QB hit allowed and a 66.7 PFF run-block grade. One game does not establish unit quality; pass-block and run-block performance must be evaluated separately.
gameWatch.risk: Protection problems could keep Gibbs blocking rather than running routes. A move to 4.5 changes the question materially; no playable cutoff has been established.
gameWatch.needs: Recheck receptions and receiving yards at 5:30 PM; do not treat the earlier 3.5 article as a live offer.
